task:
Create a Kubernetes deployment for a Python Flask web application with:
    - Docker image: "myapp:v1.0"
    - 3 replicas for high availability
    - Port 8080
    - CPU requests: 100m, limits: 500m
    - Memory requests: 128Mi, limits: 512Mi
    - Environment variables: DEBUG=false, LOG_LEVEL=info
    - Auto-scaling: min 2, max 10 replicas based on 70% CPU utilization
    - Include liveness and readiness probes
    - Namespace: production
plan_summary: Create a Kubernetes deployment YAML file with the specified requirements, then apply it using the kubectl command-line tool. The deployment will include a container based on the myapp:v1.0 Docker image, with 3 initial replicas for high availability. The container will listen on port 8080 and have the specified CPU and memory requests and limits. Environment variables will be set as specified. An auto-scaling configuration will be added to scale the deployment based on CPU utilization. Liveness and readiness probes will be included to ensure the application is running correctly. The deployment will be created in the production namespace.
review_issues: The imagePullPolicy is set to IfNotPresent, which may lead to using outdated images if the image is updated
The deployment does not have a rolling update strategy defined
The service type is set to ClusterIP, which may not be suitable for external access
There is no ingress resource defined for external access
The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler does not have a behavior defined for scaling down
review_strengths: The deployment has a liveness probe and a readiness probe defined
The deployment has resource requests and limits defined
The deployment has a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler defined for scaling
The deployment has a defined number of replicas for high availability
